about: Wrong answers that point to a specific misunderstanding about exponents, roots and scientific notation. 'pointsTo' is the subskill to work on. Claude's draft (2026-11-21), waiting for owner review.

misconceptions.description: Multiplies the exponents when multiplying powers: x³ · x⁴ = x¹² (they add).
Divides the exponents when dividing powers: x⁶ / x² = x³ (they subtract).
Adds the exponents when dividing: x⁶ / x² = x⁸.
Subtracts the exponents the wrong way round: x² / x⁶ = x⁴.
Adds the exponents for a power of a power: (x²)³ = x⁵ (they multiply).
Thinks a negative exponent makes the number negative: 2⁻³ = −8.
Multiplies the base by the exponent: 2⁻³ = −6.
Keeps the negative sign when moving the power to the bottom: x⁻⁴ = 1/x⁻⁴.
Ignores the negative exponent's flip: (2/3)⁻² = 4/9 (it's 9/4).
Thinks anything to the 0 power is 0 (it's 1).
Thinks a number to the 0 power is the number itself (7⁰ = 7; it's 1).
Halves instead of taking the square root: √64 = 32.
Divides by 3 for a cube root: ∛27 = 9.
Drops the sign of a cube root of a negative number: ∛−8 = 2 (it's −2).
Thinks every square root is irrational (√16 = 4 is rational).
Thinks a repeating decimal (0.333…) is irrational; it's a fraction, so it's rational.
Thinks π is rational (3.14 is only close to π).
Gets the sign of the exponent wrong: small numbers (less than 1) have negative exponents.
Counts the zeros instead of the places the point moves: 45000 = 4.5 × 10³.
Writes a number in front that isn't between 1 and 10: 32 × 10⁵.
Moves the decimal point the wrong way: 3.2 × 10³ = 0.0032.
Writes as many zeros as the exponent after the digits: 4.5 × 10³ = 45000 (it's 4500).
